headline: Kai, markets priced a Hormuz reopening all week; over the weekend Iran raised the price.
subline: A missile targeted an ADNOC tanker Saturday, Riyadh, Ankara and Islamabad signed a NATO-style pact, and July CPI lands Wednesday.
asof: Weekend edition · markets closed · index, yield, gold and Brent figures are Friday's close (Aug 7); bitcoin as of ~6:40 AM ET Sunday · every figure links to its source below

items.title: The jobs miss was broader than the headline
items.sentence: July payrolls fell 23,000 against an expected 80,000 gain, prior months lost another 100,000 to revisions, and unemployment fell to 4.1% only because participation shrank, per STL.News.

items.title: Rate-hike bets keep draining away
items.sentence: The 10-year yield eased 3 basis points to 4.65% Friday as the jobs data scaled back bets on Fed rate hikes, per Trading Economics, with the September meeting now the open question CPI will help settle.

items.title: Gold closes the week at $4,343
items.sentence: Spot gold rose 2.44% Friday to $4,343.43 an ounce and is up 27.79% over the past year, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Brent gave back 7% this week
items.sentence: Brent settled Friday at $83.55, up 1.29% on the day but down about 7% on the week as Hormuz reopening talks progressed, per Trading Economics — Saturday's tanker incident is the first test of that optimism.

items.title: Bitcoin sits out the drama near $64,900
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades at $64,910 this morning, essentially flat over 24 hours, per Coinbase.

items.title: Iran: strait stays shut until US 'corrects' behavior
items.sentence: The Oman deal is still a negotiation, not a reopening — fewer than 10 ships a day are transiting under a proposed model that routes entries through Iranian waters and exits through Omani ones, per CBS News.

items.title: Missile targets ADNOC vessel inside Hormuz
items.sentence: Abu Dhabi's national oil company said one of its ships was targeted Saturday while transiting the strait, with no injuries reported, per CBS News.

items.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan sign defense pact
items.sentence: The Mecca Joint Deterrence Agreement establishes mutual-defense obligations similar to NATO's Article 5, per CBS News, and Iranian officials dismissed it within hours.

items.title: Senate confirms Todd Blanche as attorney general
items.sentence: The 50-49 vote came early Saturday morning, installing Trump's former personal lawyer atop the Justice Department, per NPR.

items.title: Senate passes Russia energy-tariff bill
items.sentence: The measure allows steep new tariffs on major importers of Russian energy and passed Friday in honor of the late Lindsey Graham, who championed it, per NPR.

items.title: Hassabis steps back; Jeff Dean leaves Google
items.sentence: Demis Hassabis is shifting from day-to-day DeepMind operations to broader scientific leadership while longtime chief scientist Jeff Dean departs to launch a startup automating scientific research, per Tech Startups.

items.title: Tesla and SpaceX commit $16.8 billion to chips
items.sentence: The two companies are funding Terafab, a Texas semiconductor plant spanning roughly 100 million square feet for chip manufacturing and testing, per Tech Startups.

items.title: ByteDance trains a 10-trillion-parameter model
items.sentence: The run is roughly three times larger than competing frontier systems, an attempt to close the gap with US labs despite chip export controls, per Tech Startups.

items.title: OpenAI and Jony Ive plan 2027 speaker
items.sentence: OpenAI's first device with Ive's studio is a hockey-puck-sized, battery-powered smart speaker priced above $300 and slated for 2027, per Tech Startups.

items.title: Data centers become a campaign issue
items.sentence: Candidates in both parties are now running on data-center moratoria in state elections, per NPR, which notes the issue is gaining prominence heading into the midterms.
